title: Motorola Razr 70 Plus
description: notebookcheck review of the Motorola Razr Plus 2026. This slightly lighter, slightly faster, and higher-memory clamshell-style foldable is put through its paces in our test lab.

The absolute highlight: The removable 5,300 mAh battery, which can be charged via 30W fast charging or wirelessly. Thanks to its rugged, IP68-certified housing, a high-resolution 64 MP triple camera, and future-proof Android.

A whopping 12GB of RAM and 512GB of storage round out this top-of-the-line phone.

Beneath the massive 8-inch display lie pure high-end specs, such as the Snapdragon 8 Elite processor, a 200-megapixel camera, and a long-lasting 5,000-mAh silicon battery. Our review will determine whether the Samsung phone is worth its price tag of over $2,000 and if it’s worth buying.

The affordable Xiaomi smartphone also offers 67 W HyperCharge, 256 GB of storage, 5G and a Snapdragon 6s Gen 4 processor. A 50 MP dual camera rounds out the package, but our review reveals some surprising weaknesses.

title: Apple iPhone 18 Pro
description: Review| How good is the iPhone 18 Pro really? Our review tests the new A20 Pro, the 6.3-inch OLED with 120 Hz, the 48 MP camera with variable aperture, as well as battery life, performance, PWM and display. We also assess the Apple phone's features, build quality and everyday usability, and show who Apple's Pro iPhone is worth buying for.

title: Xiaomi Poco X8
description: notebookcheck.com review of the Xiaomi Poco X8. This phone, closely related to the Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G and featuring plenty of storage and an IP68 rating, could be one of the best phone deals of 2026 when it comes to display and battery life.

title: Xiaomi 18 Fold
description: Xiaomi 18 Fold review: How good are its OLED displays, Xring processor, cameras and battery? Our lab test reveals both strengths and weaknesses.

title: Xiaomi Redmi 17 5G
description: notebookcheck.com review of the Xiaomi Redmi 17 5G. This budget-friendly mobile phone truly is is an impressive endurance front runner. Are you looking to buy a phone that is both affordable and offers a long-lasting battery? Well, if that's the case, you’ve come to the right place.

title: Xiaomi Redmi Note 17 5G
description: In our review, the Xiaomi Redmi Note 17 5G impressed with its exceptional battery life, but disappointed with a weaker SoC, a stripped-down camera, and less RAM.

title: Xiaomi Redmi Note 17 Pro Max 5G
description: Xiaomi Redmi Note 17 Pro Max 5G review: A massive 9,210 mAh battery, extreme ruggedness, and a bright AMOLED display. Is it worth your money, despite the weak Snapdragon processor?

title: OnePlus 16
description: notebookcheck.com review of the OnePlus 16. Unfortunately, this fast phone with plenty of storage and a large battery is not officially coming to Europe or the USA. Nevertheless, it is an interesting device at a good price as an imported smartphone.

title: Oppo Find X7 Ultra
description: The Oppo Find X7 Ultra is a 6.82-inch smartphone that is equipped with a Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 and its internal Adreno 750 GPU, up to 16 GB of LPDDR5X RAM, and 512 GB UFS 4.0 storage. The fast 120 Hz LTPO AMOLED display has a resolution of 3168x1440 pixels, reaching a pixel density of 510 PPI. Other equipment characteristics are a 50-MP quad-camera system that was set up together with Hasselblad and uses the 1-inch Sony LYT-900 sensor, WiFi 7, Bluetooth 5.4, and ColorOS based on Android 14. The 5000-mAh battery can be recharged at up to 100 watts. Wireless charging and reverse wireless charging are also supported.

title: Bigme Hibreak
description: Are e-ink displays too slow for normal use? Bigme aims to dispel this prejudice by proving you should be able to use the HiBreak as a normal smartphone and simultaneously enjoy all the benefits of electronic paper. But can the HiBreak also display videos in an acceptable manner?

title: Honor Watch 5 Ultra
description: The Honor Watch 5 Ultra is set to score big with features like the titanium casing, LTPO AMOLED display, and ceramic feel. The new top model is also said to be durable and is approved for diving. We take the Watch 5 Ultra for a test drive and see how it fares.

title: Huawei Watch Fit 4 Pro
description: With the Watch Fit 4 Pro, Huawei has expanded its smartwatch portfolio with a premium outdoor sports model that impresses not only with high-quality and robust materials, but also a bright display and long battery life.

title: Huawei Watch 5
description: The Huawei Watch 5 presents itself as a high-quality smartwatch in our test, offering convincing optics and technology. The new X-Tap sensor as well as the gesture control represent only a couple of the innovations brought by the Watch 5. Additionally, it impresses with a good battery life in our test.

title: Amazfit Active 2
description: The Active 2 from Amazfit is excellently equipped and works flawlessly in everyday life. It shines brightly, measures accurately and is smart. Why should you spend more money on a smartwatch?

title: Xiaomi Smart Band 10
description: More display, more brightness, more money. The Smart Band 10 has become better and more expensive. It is now supposed to measure sleep efficiency, improve swimming training and measure body values even more precisely thanks to AI support. We have tried it out.

title: Huawei Watch GT 6 Pro
description: Review | The Huawei Watch GT 6 Pro features higher-quality materials, adds an ECG function, and provides access to exclusive sports modes. New sensors promise even more precise measurements, and the battery capacity has increased noticeably.

title: Huawei Watch GT 6
description: Test | The Huawei Watch GT 6 comes with a significantly larger battery and continues to deliver highly accurate sensor readings. Huawei has also expanded the feature set, with major upgrades for cycling in particular. Read on for the full review.

title: Samsung Galaxy Watch8
description: With the Samsung Galaxy Watch8, Google's Gemini AI assistant arrives at the wrist. In addition, the 2025 version of the smartwatch is significantly brighter. Our test shows what the Galaxy Watch8 LTE can do.

title: Samsung Galaxy Watch8 Classic
description: Samsung has introduced another Classic model in the Galaxy Watch8 series. The Classic’s defining feature is its rotating bezel, but it also inherits the extra button and design cues from the Ultra. Our review examines whether the price premium for the Classic is truly worth it.

title: Hilo Band
description: Hilo Band review | The Hilo Band is a compact health tracker that monitors blood pressure around the clock and can do so for two weeks on a single battery charge. The device is medically certified and offers smart features, but it also revealed a few weaknesses in our review.

title: Apple Watch Series 11 42mm
description: The Watch Series 11 comes with an optional titanium case and 5G chip. It should be able to detect high blood pressure, automatically recognize workouts, warn of noise and call the emergency services in the event of an accident. The Apple Watch is a jack-of-all-trades and a classic - we tried out the 11th generation.

title: Huawei Watch Ultimate 2
description: A smartwatch rated for dives up to 150 meters, designed for the golf course and demanding expeditions, all wrapped in an elegant design. Huawei’s Watch Ultimate 2 aims to excel across multiple scenarios. Our test reveals whether it truly delivers.

title: Amazfit T-Rex 3 Pro
description: In the test, the Amazfit T-Rex 3 Pro impressed with its bright and large AMOLED, offline navigation and all kinds of health and fitness features. Our test report reveals what else the robust smartwatch has to offer.

title: Huawei Watch GT Runner 2
description: The Huawei Watch GT Runner 2 is clearly designed for runners and aims to impress with its lightweight titanium case, precise multi-band GNSS, long battery life, and numerous training features. The main question in this review is whether it’s more than just a successful update or whether it truly ranks among the top running watches.

title: Huawei Watch Fit 5 Pro
description: With the Watch Fit 5 and Watch Fit 5 Pro, Huawei is once again taking on Apple, Samsung, and Garmin. These smartwatches offer high-quality displays, long battery life, and extensive fitness features at attractive prices. However, our review reveals that not everything shines in everyday use. We examine their strengths and weaknesses and consider whether they’re really worth buying.

title: Amazfit Cheetah 2 Pro
description: We're testing the Amazfit Cheetah 2 Pro, a potential alternative to Garmin Forerunner and Fenix smartwatches, for example. The watch impresses with its great features and features a relatively compact display.

title: Xiaomi Smart Band 10 Pro
description: Better than a fitness tracker but not quite a smartwatch yet? Xiaomi’s Smart Band 10 Pro fills that gap. Its strengths are its accurate readings and its bright AMOLED display.

title: RingConn Gen 3
description: RingConn Gen 3 review: Up to 14 days of battery life, vibration, and no subscription! How does the smart ring perform in everyday use? Read about all its strengths and weaknesses here.

title: Huawei Watch GT 7
description: Huawei Watch GT 7 Review: We test the 41- and 46-mm versions for battery life, fitness and health features, GPS, and everyday usability. Which GT 7 model performs better?

title: Huawei Watch GT 7 Pro
description: Offline navigation, mobile payments, an extremely bright display, and a titanium case. The Huawei Watch GT 7 Pro is designed to do it all and is aimed particularly at skiers and cyclists. We put it to the test.

title: Huawei Watch D3
description: We’re testing the Huawei Watch D3, a smartwatch that features accurate blood pressure measurement using a cuff and micro-pump, an ECG, and many health features.

title: Xiaomi Watch S5
description: Xiaomi Watch S5 Review: The smartwatch impresses with a long-lasting battery, precise GNSS, and a high-quality AMOLED display. However, there are some drawbacks when it comes to apps and smartwatch features.

title: Samsung Galaxy Watch9
description: Samsung Galaxy Watch9 Review: How Good Is the New Samsung Smartwatch? Discover all the specs and highlights in this review: brilliant AMOLED display, long battery life, precise GPS, and advanced health tracking (heart rate & sleep). Add to that a sleek, rugged design with intuitive controls. Read the detailed review with test data now and find out if it’s worth buying!

title: Honor Watch 6
description: Honor Watch 6 Review: How Good Are the Battery, GPS, and Heart Rate Monitoring? We also test the new sports modes for soccer and badminton.

title: Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra2
description: 5000 cd/m². That’s how bright the display of the new Samsung Galaxy Ultra2 is in our test. It measures accurately, offers lots of apps and analytics, and lasts a long time for a Wear OS smartwatch. Our test.

title: Huawei Watch 6 Pro
description: Huawei Watch 6 Pro Space Edition review: How good are its health features, GPS, display and battery life? Is it worth upgrading from the Watch 5?

title: Amazfit Balance
description: Amazfit promises all kinds of AI features for its Balance. We thoroughly tested the new smartwatch with numerous health and wellness features. Our Amazfit Balance review reveals everything the wearable has to offer.

title: Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra
description: More battery life, titanium casing, multisport support. Samsung wants to offer more of everything with the Galaxy Watch Ultra. We take a look at the top model.

title: Garmin Fenix 8 Solar
description: The Garmin Fenix 8 Solar is a high-quality smartwatch with an extremely long battery life. Read the Notebookcheck test report to find out whether the Fenix 8 is worth buying.

title: Amazfit Helio Ring
description: Amazfit Helio Ring impressed us with its high-quality materials, low weight, long battery life, and comprehensive health tracking—all at a comparatively low price. Even if it cannot keep all its promises, it still delivers a coherent overall picture.

title: Samsung Galaxy Tab A11+
description: Notebookcheck reviews the Samsung Galaxy Tab A11 Plus 5G that offers a MediaTek Dimensity 7300 SoC, 6 GB RAM, and 128 GB storage for under €300.

title: Teclast T60 Pro
description: notebookcheck.com review of the Teclast T60 Pro. The large tablet with a 12-inch screen is also a very affordable pad and still offers features that are partly on a par with an iPad Pro: Aluminum casing, pen support and LTE support.

title: Xiaomi Poco Pad M1
description: In the test, the Poco Pad M1 aims to impress with its flicker-free 12.1-inch display, fast SoC, Dolby Atmos speakers and large battery. Read on to find out what else it has to offer.

title: Huawei MatePad 11.5 S (2026)
description: Notebookcheck reviews the Huawei MatePad 11.5 S (2026). As always with a Huawei device, the question arises as to whether HarmonyOS without Google Services is sufficient for everyday use. We also take a closer look at the matte screen with pen support.

title: Xiaomi Poco Pad X1
description: In our review, the Xiaomi Poco Pad X1 impressed us with its flicker-free 144Hz display, fast SoC, ample storage, and high-quality accessories. Is it a bargain, or are there a few bitter pils to swallow?

title: Lenovo Tab K9
description: Notebookcheck reviews the Lenovo Tab K9, an Android business tablet designed for simple work. It is so handy that you can easily take it with you. If you are looking for an affordable and compact tablet, you could also be happy with it for personal use.

title: Lenovo Tab K11 Gen 2
description: Notebookcheck reviews the Lenovo Tab K11 Gen 2, a mid-range Android tablet that is almost exactly the same as the Lenovo Idea Tab. However, the Tab K11 Gen 2 does have a few discernable differences of its own.

title: Lenovo Tab K12
description: notebookcheck.com review of the Lenovo Tab K12. The tablet for business customers could also be interesting for private users because it has many features that have become rare: For example, this is a tablet with a charger included.

title: Apple iPad Air 11 M4 2026
description: notebookcheck.com review of the Apple iPad Air 11 M4 from 2026. Apple's mid-range tablet would be considered a high-end tablet in the Android segment and delivers nearly as much power as the high-end tablets of recent years. Does this make it a top-tier tablet?

title: Apple iPad Air 13 M4 2026
description: notebookcheck review of the Apple iPad Air 13 M4 2026 8th generation. The large tablet defies the RAM crisis and comes with 12 GB of RAM, i.e. plenty of memory despite high global market prices. Upgrades for data storage are still very expensive at Apple, but prices have fallen significantly overall, at least in Europe.

title: Lenovo Legion Tab 5 (Legion Y700 Gen5)
description: notebookcheck tests the Lenovo Legion Tab 5 TB323FU 2026, also known as Legion Y700 Gen 5. The handy gaming tablet can also compete with gaming handhelds, and even has an emulator for PC games installed.

title: Lenovo Idea Tab Pro Gen 2
description: notebookcheck.com test of the Lenovo Idea Tab Pro Gen 2. The slim 13-inch tablet with pen input is sometimes available for less than 500 euros. It can impress with AI features, but is perhaps not the ideal choice for everyone due to its rather moderate runtimes? We find out in the test.

title: Honor MagicPad 4
description: Honor MagicPad4 review | Powered by a Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 processor, the 12.3-inch tablet features a 165Hz OLED screen and ultra-thin bezels. Read Notebookcheck's review and discover if this large Android tablet is worth your hard-earned cash.

title: Lenovo ThinkTab X11
description: ThinkPad X11 review | This waterproof Android tablet features a Qualcomm Snapdragon 7s Gen 3 processor and two USB-C ports. Read Notebookcheck's review to find out if the ThinkPad X11, with its rugged MIL-STD-810H and IP69 certifications, is worth its asking price and comes as a recommended purchase.

title: Oppo Pad Mini
description: Review: Oppo Pad Mini | Oppo’s new compact and lightweight tablet is one of the best alternatives to the iPad Mini. Thanks to the Snapdragon 8 Gen 5, this small tablet delivers powerful performance. Read the Pad Mini review to find out if it’s worth buying.

title: Durabook R10
description: The Durabook R10 is a true heavyweight designed for extreme working environments. With a solid magnesium chassis, brightness exceeding 1,000 cd/m², and a clever hot-swap battery system, the Durabook R10 is well-suited for rugged outdoor use.

title: Oppo Pad 5 Pro
description: Review| The Oppo Pad 5 Pro combines a slim metal body with a massive 13,380-mAh battery and 67-W fast charging. The Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5, up to 16 GB of LPDDR5X RAM, and 512 GB of UFS 4.1 storage ensure high performance. The 13.2-inch IPS display in a 7:5 aspect ratio offers 3,392 × 2,400 pixels, a 144 Hz refresh rate, 1,000 nits of brightness, and 98% DCI-P3 coverage. Eight speakers, Wi-Fi 7, USB-C at 5 Gbit/s, an optional Magic Keyboard-style keyboard case, and ColorOS 16 based on Android 16 make this tablet a premium all-rounder.

title: OnePlus Pad 4
description: NotebookCheck review of the OnePlus Pad 4. This large tablet from OnePlus, available at an affordable price, is likely one of the manufacturer’s last devices to be released in Europe. It’s a tablet that offers excellent value for the price, which is why it’s a shame that the manufacturer is bowing out.

title: Oppo Pad 5
description: Review | The Oppo Pad 5 is available with Wi-Fi or 5G. While the Chinese version is provided with the powerful Dimensity 9400+, the global model uses the considerably slower Dimensity 7300. It also features a 10,050 mAh battery with 33 W charging and a 12.1-inch IPS display with a resolution of 2,800 × 1,980 pixels, a 120 Hz refresh rate and a claimed brightness of 900 nits. Compared with the Chinese model, both the display resolution and charging speed have been reduced, significantly weakening the tablet's overall appeal.

title: Huawei MatePad Pro Max
description: Huawei MatePad Pro Max review: We put its display, performance, battery life, software, and accessories to the test and find out whether this XXL tablet can actually replace a laptop.

title: Lenovo Tab Plus Gen 2
description: Nine speakers, a dedicated subwoofer, and Dolby Atmos support ensure that the sound on the Lenovo Tab Plus Gen 2 will blow you away. Hardly any other tablet can keep up. Plus, Lenovo has come up with a new built-in stand that works brilliantly. So, is it the perfect entertainment device?

title: Xiaomi Redmi Pad 2 9.7
description: The new Xiaomi Redmi Pad 2 9.7, with its 120 Hz 2K display, promises true premium features at a budget price under 200 euros. But how does this compact 9.7-inch Android tablet fare in our test? We put the Xiaomi tablet to the test with its bright screen and just under 4 GB of RAM. Our in-depth review covers performance, battery life, and test results. It also supports stylus use.

title: Lenovo Yoga Tab Gen 2
description: notebookcheck.com review of the Yoga Tab Gen 2. This high-end tablet costs around 650 euros and impresses with innovative features such as eye tracking. It also comes with numerous AI features and is a Lenovo tablet with a stylus.

title: Huawei MatePad Air (2026)
description: The Huawei MatePad Air (2026) is a new Android tablet that emphasizes slim design and a low-reflection display, thanks to its "PaperMatte" technology. The device itself is 5.3 mm thick and weighs 509 grams. It features a 12-inch OLED screen complete with a matte coating that reduces glare—both indoors and outdoors—and provides tactile, paper-like resistance when used with the M-Pencil Pro. The tablet is powered by a 10,100 mAh battery and runs on Huawei’s proprietary operating system, HarmonyOS 4.3.

title: Xiaomi Pad 9 Pro Max
description: Review | The Xiaomi Pad 9 Pro Max represents the absolute pinnacle of performance in the tablet segment. Equipped with a 13.3-inch 3.4K display featuring a 144 Hz refresh rate and 1,000 nits of brightness, it delivers PC-level capabilities. Its proprietary Xring O3 3nm processor, combined with up to 16 GB of LPDDR6 RAM and 1 TB of storage ensures outstanding performance. A massive 12,000 mAh battery with 120W fast charging, a DisplayPort video input, and HyperOS 4 round off this 5.67 mm thin flagship.

title: Lenovo Yoga Tab Plus Gen 2
description: Notebookcheck.com review of the Lenovo Yoga Tab Plus Gen 2. This fast, powerful 13-inch tablet looks great, and Lenovo has also fitted a large battery. The Lenovo Yoga Tab Plus Gen 2 can be purchased directly from the manufacturer, although other online retailers often offer lower prices.

title: Xiaomi Pad 9
description: Review | Xiaomi Pad 9 Review: Can this price-performance standout—priced under $500—beat the Apple iPad 11? We put the new Android tablet through its paces, featuring an 11.2-inch 144Hz display, a Snapdragon 8s Gen 4 processor, and a premium feature set that includes a stylus. At Notebookcheck, we evaluate this affordable iPad Air alternative for both productivity and entertainment.

title: Huawei MatePad Paper
description: Our experts test the MatePad Paper. At first glance, you might think that it is an e-reader, but you will quickly notice that the tablet can do much more. With Android apps on an E Ink display, the multitude of options gets really interesting.

title: Lenovo Smart Paper
description: The Smart Paper is a high-quality e-ink tablet made by Lenovo which you can use for easy note taking and to help you study documents without getting tired. Although the device is based on Android, you can hardly run any apps on it. In this review, we will find out about what the tablet can and can't do.

title: Google Pixel Tablet
description: The Pixel Tablet is an interesting alternative to the Galaxy Tab S9 or Apple iPad. Read on as our Notebookcheck review reveals whether the Google tablet is a worthwhile purchase.

title: Onyx Boox Note Air 3 C
description: The Note Air 3 C from Onyx Boox is an e-ink tablet that is great as an e-reader and also works with Android apps, allowing you to expand its functionality. We take a closer look at the qualities and possible disadvantages in the test.

title: Onyx Boox Tab Ultra C Pro
description: Of course, you can read books in color on the Onyx Boox Tab Ultra C Pro, but you can also do so much more than that: Thanks to pen input, you can draw or take notes, thanks to the Android system, you can run apps, and you can even take pictures. But there are also some limitations ...

title: Onyx Boox Page
description: At just 7 inches, the Onyx Boox Page is a very handy e-reader that uses Android as its operating system. Reading on the display is really fun, but can you also use other apps on a black and white display with a slow response time?

title: PocketBook InkPad Color 3
description: The InkPad Color 3 has an e-ink color display and supports borrowing e-books from libraries. Thanks to the speaker and Bluetooth you can also play audiobooks. However, the proprietary software makes the e-reader somewhat inflexible.

title: Onyx Boox Palma
description: The Onyx Boox Palma looks like a cell phone but lacks essential functions such as mobile communications. So it's more of a very handy e-book reader with Android app support and even a small camera. Find out what you can do with the Palma in our test.

title: Onyx Boox Note Air 3
description: The Onyx Boox Note Air 3 with a Snapdragon 680 and Android 12 aims to win over buyers with its pen input, large display, and stylish metal casing. Can the version with the black and white e-Ink-Carta display convince us like its cousin with a color display?

title: Onyx Boox TabX
description: At 13.3 inches, the Onyx Boox Tab X is one of the largest e-ink tablets on the market. Thanks to the Android operating system, it offers app support and therefore enables a wide range of applications. Find out how the tablet fared in our test here.

title: PocketBook Era Color
description: The PocketBook Era Color features a 7-inch color e-ink display which sits inside quite a small case, making it easy to take with you on the go. Plus, you can even charge it wirelessly thanks to its great accessories. We took a closer look at the compact e-reader.

title: PocketBook Verse Pro Color
description: With its 6-inch, color e-ink display and Bluetooth for connecting speakers or headphones, you can use the PocketBook Verse Pro Color to enjoy both e-books, comics and even audiobooks. Does the cheap and portable e-reader do enough to impress in our review?

title: PocketBook Color Note
description: Thanks to a large e-ink screen that can display colors, the PocketBook Color Note is perfect for browsing through books, writing notes and drawing. It also comes with a stylus. So, does everything work fine? Not quite because unfortunately, the manufacturer has made one fatal decision...
